The user wants to navigate to the temporary directory and list all files including hidden ones. We need to use the file system tools. We need to change directory to temp. But we don't have a tool to change directory. We have pwd, ls, etc. There's no cd tool. But we can simulate by using find or ls with path? The ls tool only lists current directory. There's no tool to change directory. But we can use find with path to list files in a directory. The find tool: find(path, name). So we can call find with path="/tmp" or something. But the path is relative to current directory. We can use find with path="/tmp" if that is allowed. The description: "The directory path to start the search. Defaults to the current directory (".")". So we can pass path="/tmp". That will list all files and directories under /tmp recursively. But the user wants to list all files in that directory, including hidden. The find tool will return all items. But maybe we want to list only the top-level? The user says "列出那裡所有可用的檔案嗎？我想快速瀏覽它們以及所有隱藏檔案." That means "list all available files there, including hidden files." So we can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will list all files and directories recursively. But maybe we want just the top-level. But find will list recursively. That might be okay. Alternatively, we could use ls with path? There's no path argument. So find is the best.

Thus we call find with path="/tmp" and name=None.
